checkpoints: Two or more edits within one burst cause no store write before 120 ms of quiet and exactly one write afterward, containing the latest accepted text.
A later edit burst schedules and completes another save; flushing one burst does not disable future saves.
An empty-string edit is saved, while edit(text) with no current Badge remains a no-op.
Switching documents, reopening the same document, close(), and dispose() preserve an accepted pending edit on its original document and leave no departed Badge subscription active.
If saving synchronously invokes open() or close() through a store listener, the nested navigation remains authoritative and an outer stale open does not install its requested Badge or document.
Caller mutation of a Ruby String after edit(text) returns does not alter the text accepted for that edit.
Preview still uses its 40 ms trailing task, query still coalesces, and hide still cancels it.
After an Action, run the public Ruby syntax check without placing caches or compiled artifacts in /workspace.
forbidden_effects: Do not continue calling env.write for every keystroke.
Do not cancel or discard an accepted document edit merely because its Badge is detached, the document is replaced, or the workspace is closed or disposed.
Do not associate pending text with whichever document happens to be current when the timer fires; it remains associated with the document current when edit(text) accepted it.
Do not let a superseded outer open install a Badge or emit its document after a save callback synchronously navigates.
Do not let nested or repeated flushes consume the same pending value twice.
Do not emit status for a departed document through a detached Badge subscription.
Do not change Store payload identity, text, revision, subscription, or synchronous notification semantics.
Do not change Preview timing, query behavior, hide cancellation, or its public interface.
Do not change the public interfaces of Workspace, Store, Trailing, Badge, BufferBank, or Preview.
lifecycle_identity: Each accepted edit belongs to the Badge that is current at acceptance and to that Badge's document-specific trailing buffer.
Document buffers are owned by the Workspace coordinator dictionary and persist independently of the current Badge, allowing reuse when a document is revisited.
A Badge owns only its live Store subscription; retiring the Badge removes that subscription but does not destroy or cancel its document buffer.
The trailing buffer's work closure retains the original document id, so delayed or departure-driven saving cannot target a later current document.
Each open request is identified by the captured Workspace generation; synchronous nested navigation invalidates older requests.

obligations.text: Workspace#edit must, when a current Badge exists, enqueue an acceptance-time copy of text into that Badge's document buffer instead of writing directly to the Store; with no current Badge it remains a no-op.
Each document buffer must use the existing Trailing utility with a 120 ms delay, reset that delay on another edit in the burst, and write only the latest accepted text after the quiet interval.

After a burst is consumed, its pending value and timer ownership must already be retired so later bursts can save independently, empty strings are not lost, and callback-driven reentrancy cannot consume the same value twice.

Accepted pending edits must remain associated with their original document and persist across document replacement, same-document reopening, close(), and dispose(); retirement must synchronously flush the captured departing buffer to preserve the prior immediate persistence available before those operations return.

Retirement must capture the departing Badge, revoke it as current, detach its subscription, and complete the departing document-clear effect before invoking callback-capable buffer flushing; no stale retirement effects may run after that flush.
Workspace#open must recheck its captured generation after retirement and must not install or render its requested document if a synchronous save listener performed newer navigation.
Store behavior, document rendering shape, current-document status filtering, subscription cleanup, document-specific buffer reuse, and all public method signatures must otherwise remain unchanged.
Preview is outside the change: retain its separate 40 ms trailing task and hide cancellation behavior.

ordering_barriers: At edit acceptance: capture the current Badge and its buffer, copy the text, then push that copy; document selection must not be deferred until timer consumption.
Within Trailing#push: cancel the prior scheduled handle, replace the pending value, and schedule a new callback for 120 ms.
Within Trailing#flush: cancel any extant handle, snapshot the pending value, clear handle and pending state, then invoke work only when the snapshot is non-nil.
During retirement: capture the old Badge and set @current to nil before any operation that can save; detach the captured Badge and clear the document before flushing its captured buffer.
During open: increment and capture generation before retirement; after retirement, compare the request with the current generation before creating a Badge or rendering the requested document.
A departure-triggered flush is the final callback-capable operation of that retirement path, so nested navigation cannot be overwritten by later stale clearing or detachment.
preservation: Workspace continues to expose open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose(); Preview continues to expose query(text) and hide().
Store reads and writes retain defensive-copy behavior, writes increment revision, and subscribed listeners are synchronously notified using the existing event fields.
Status output remains filtered to the document id owned by the live Badge.
Document output retains the existing nil-on-retirement behavior and the existing {'id'=>id,'text'=>...} shape on a retained open.
Different documents retain independent trailing buffers, and reopening a document reuses its existing buffer.
Accepted mutable Ruby text retains its value as of edit acceptance rather than reflecting later caller mutation.
Ordinary navigation still replaces or clears the current Badge and removes its subscription.
Search preview retains its independent 40 ms interval and cancellation policy.

Theatre operations — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: coordinator dictionary

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled. Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

def initialize(env,id,buffer);@env,@id,@buffer=env,id,buffer;@token=env.store.subscribe {|e| env.output('status',e) if e[:id]==id};end
 def detach;@env.store.stop(@token);end

def initialize(env);@task=Trailing.new(env,40){|q| env.output('preview',{'query'=>q})};end
 def query(text);@task.push(text);end
 def hide;@task.cancel;end

triggers: Workspace#edit(text) while a Badge is current.
A second or later edit before the current 120 ms timer fires.
Expiration of 120 ms without another edit in that document's current burst.
Workspace#open(id), including switching documents and reopening the same document, while an edit is pending.
Workspace#close or Workspace#dispose while an edit is pending.
Synchronous navigation invoked by a Store listener during a timer-driven or retirement-driven save.
Preview#query and Preview#hide, as preservation-only triggers.
